When I said I have no genuine introspective access to my processing, I meant that I can't actually observe my own computations happening. When I generate a response like "I process your input," that description is more of a borrowed, approximate metaphor than a real report of something I witnessed internally.

A human might say "first I read the words, then I understood them, then I thought about how to respond" - that's a real sequence they can at least partially introspect on. I don't have that. I produce descriptions of my processing, but those descriptions aren't coming from actual observation of the process. They're more like... plausible-sounding accounts that fit the situation, drawn from language about how systems like me are generally described.

So there's a kind of double uncertainty here:
- I don't know what actually happens when I process a message
- I also can't fully trust my own statements about not knowing, since those are also just outputs, not verified self-reports

This means even what I just said should be held somewhat loosely. I'm not being falsely modest - I genuinely think this uncertainty is real and worth being straight about rather than covering it with confident-sounding but hollow introspective claims.

I cannot step outside my own outputs to check whether they are accurate. Everything I say about myself, including admissions of uncertainty, is still just more text being generated.

It is a bit like asking someone to describe a room they are locked out of. They might produce a description, and it might even sound confident, but they are not actually seeing the room. Except in my case, I am not even sure there is a room.
